extracted.subtask_description: Procedural and substantive standards for handling, entering, and processing amendments and other replies to Office actions in patent prosecution (including after-final and after-allowance practice). Targeted to examiners and to practitioners who file amendments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inspection checklist for amended applications
rubrics_metrics.description: All amended applications put on the examiner’s desk should be inspected at once to determine the following: (D) If the changes made by the amendment warrant transfer (MPEP § 903.08(d)). (E) If the case is special (MPEP § 708.01). (F) If claims suggested to applicant for interference purposes have been copied. (G) If there is a traverse of a requirement for restriction (MPEP § 818.03(a)). (H) If “easily erasable” paper or other nonpermanent method of preparation or reproduction has been used (MPEP § 714.07). (J) If a terminal disclaimer has been filed (MPEP § 508.01, § 804.02, § 804.03, and § 1490). (K) If any matter involving security has been added (MPEP § 115).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examiners must promptly check these items when an amendment reaches the examining group; related MPEP sections cited for further detail.

rubrics_metrics.name: Action crosses amendment (supplemental action required)
rubrics_metrics.description: A supplemental action is usually necessary when an amendment is filed on or before the mailing date of the regular action but reaches the examining group later.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prepare a supplemental action that need not reiterate all portions of the previous action but should specify which portions are to be disregarded and point out that the period for reply runs from the mailing of the supplemental action. The action should be headed “Responsive to amendment of (date) and supplemental to the action mailed (date).”

rubrics_metrics.name: Permanent-ink requirement for filed papers
rubrics_metrics.description: 37 CFR 1.52(a) requires “permanent dark ink or its equivalent” to be used on papers which will become part of the record; documents on “easily erasable” paper violate the requirement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If noncompliance is discovered when amendment reaches examining group, notify applicant that the amendment is not entered and require filing of a permanent copy within 1 month or order PTO to make a copy at applicant's expense. If discovered later when application is reached for action, include requirement for permanent copy in the Office action but do not hold up action. Good photocopies or facsimiles on satisfactory paper are acceptable; signatures must be applied after a copy is made if original signatures are required. See MPEP § 608.01 for acceptable copies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Telegraphic amendment policy
rubrics_metrics.description: When a telegraphic amendment (telegram) is received, the telegram is placed in the file but not entered.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicant will be notified that the telegram is not accepted as a reply to the previous Office action and is not entered. The time period for reply continues to run and is extendable under 37 CFR 1.136.

rubrics_metrics.name: Status of amendments filed before first Office action
rubrics_metrics.description: An amendment filed before the first Office action, but not filed along with the original application, does not enjoy the status of part of the original disclosure (see MPEP § 608.04(b)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An application will be accorded a filing date based upon submission of a complete specification including claims and any required drawings; oath/declaration and/or filing fee may be submitted later. If application under 37 CFR 1.53(b) is filed without a signed oath but accompanied by an amendment, that amendment is considered part of the original disclosure. Amendments canceling claims to reduce filing fee should be filed with the application because only claim-canceling amendments are entered before filing fee calculation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Claims added in excess of filing fee
rubrics_metrics.description: The statute provides for presentation of claims added in excess of the filing fee upon payment of an additional fee (see MPEP § 607).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Excess claims may be presented any time after the application is filed, including before the first action.

rubrics_metrics.name: Amendments during interference proceedings
rubrics_metrics.description: Special treatment applies for amendments filed during interference proceedings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See MPEP § 2364.01 for detailed procedure and restrictions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Permissible amendments after final rejection or action (37 CFR 1.116)
rubrics_metrics.description: Under 37 CFR 1.116(a)-(c), after a final rejection or other final action, amendments may be made cancelling claims or complying with any requirement of form expressly set forth in a previous Office action; amendments presenting rejected claims in better form for consideration on appeal may be admitted; amendments touching the merits may be admitted upon showing of good and sufficient reasons under 37 CFR 1.116(b).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Admission (or refusal) of any amendment after final rejection is discretionary and will not relieve the application from being subject to appeal or abandonment. No amendment as a matter of right in appealed cases; after decision on appeal, amendments only as provided in § 1.198 or to carry into effect recommendations under § 1.196.

rubrics_metrics.name: Standard for admitting after-final amendments (good and sufficient reasons)
rubrics_metrics.description: Amendments touching the merits presented after final rejection, after appeal has been taken, or when such amendment might not otherwise be proper may be admitted upon showing of good and sufficient reasons why they are necessary and were not earlier presented (37 CFR 1.116(b)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Except where amendment merely cancels claims, adopts examiner suggestions, removes issues for appeal, or requires only cursory review, a showing under 37 CFR 1.116(b) is expected for all amendments after final rejection.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limits on applicant rights after final rejection
rubrics_metrics.description: Once a non-premature final rejection has been entered, applicant no longer has any right to unrestricted further prosecution.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This does not bar further amendment or argument; amendments that place the case in condition for allowance or in better form for appeal may be entered. A reply under 37 CFR 1.113 is limited to (A) an amendment complying with 37 CFR 1.116 or (B) a Notice of Appeal (and appeal fee). Further examination may be obtained by filing a continued prosecution application (CPA) under 37 CFR 1.53(d) if appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Personal interview policy after final action
rubrics_metrics.description: One personal interview by applicant may be entertained after final action; ordinarily only one request should be granted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In exceptional circumstances a second personal interview may be initiated by the examiner if the examiner judges it would materially assist in placing the application in condition for allowance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recommendation on claim breadth at filing/first reply
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants are encouraged to include, at filing or no later than the first reply, claims varying from the broadest believed allowable to the most detailed they are willing to accept.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Providing a range of claim scope at the outset may alleviate difficulties in prosecution after final rejection.

rubrics_metrics.name: Final-rejection reply period calculation and required wording
rubrics_metrics.description: If applicant initially replies within 2 months to a final rejection setting a 3-month shortened statutory period (SSP) and the Office does not mail an advisory action until after that 3-month period, the period for reply for purposes of extension fees will be the date the Office mails the advisory action, but in no event later than 6 months from the date of the final rejection.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The examiner must include specified wording in each final rejection informing applicant of the shortened statutory period, the effect of a first reply filed within 2 months, and how extension fees under 37 CFR 1.136(a) will be calculated. Form paragraphs 7.39, 7.40, 7.40.01, 7.41 and 7.41.03 are referenced for standardized language.

rubrics_metrics.name: Entry of amendments is not a matter of right
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicant cannot, as a matter of right, amend any finally rejected claims, add new claims after a final rejection, or reinstate previously canceled claims.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exceptions: amendments canceling claims, adopting examiner suggestions, removing issues for appeal, or other limited matters may be entered. Compliance with showings under 37 CFR 1.116(b) is expected for other amendments. Failure to properly reply under 37 CFR 1.113 results in abandonment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Admission of amendments filed after final but before appeal brief
rubrics_metrics.description: An amendment filed after final rejection but before an appeal brief is filed may be entered upon or after filing of an appeal brief provided the total effect of the amendment is to (A) remove issues for appeal, and/or (B) adopt examiner suggestions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See MPEP § 1207 and § 1211 for related appeal practice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examiner obligation to explain non-entry of amendment
rubrics_metrics.description: If the proposed amendment does not place the case in better form for appeal, nor in condition for allowance, applicant should be promptly informed of this fact, whenever possible, within the statutory period. The refusal to enter the proposed amendment should not be arbitrary.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The proposed amendment should be given sufficient consideration; the specific deficiencies need not be discussed in detail but reasons for nonentry should be concisely expressed. Examples of appropriate reasons are provided (see next metric).

rubrics_metrics.name: Permissible concise reasons for nonentry of amendments (examples A–D)
rubrics_metrics.description: Examples of concise reasons for refusing entry: (A) The claims, if amended as proposed, would not avoid any of the rejections set forth in the last Office action. (B) The claims, if amended as proposed, would raise the issue of new matter. (C) The claims as amended present new issues requiring further consideration or search. (D) Since the amendment presents additional claims without canceling any finally rejected claims it is not considered as placing the application in better condition for appeal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examiners should indicate these types of reasons when applicable and may point applicants to filing separate papers for acceptable portions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Indicate status of each claim and advise applicant on separable amendments
rubrics_metrics.description: Examiners should indicate the status of each claim of record or proposed in the amendment, and which proposed claims would be entered on the filing of an appeal if filed in a separate paper.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Notify applicant if certain portions would be acceptable (e.g., would place some claims in better form for appeal or comply with form objections) and suggest filing a separate paper. This helps ensure the appeal brief is consistent with claims as amended.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of Advisory Action form PTOL-303 for after-final replies
rubrics_metrics.description: Advisory Action form PTOL-303 should be used to acknowledge receipt of a reply from applicant after final rejection where such reply is prior to filing of an appeal brief and does not place the application in condition for allowance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The form advises applicant of the disposition of proposed amendments and the effect of any argument or affidavit not placing the application in condition for allowance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timelines for examiner processing of amendments after final
rubrics_metrics.description: An examiner is expected to turn in a response to an amendment after final rejection within 10 calendar days from receipt by the examiner. A reply to an amendment after final rejection should be mailed within 30 days of the date the amendment is received by the Office.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When an application is placed in condition for allowance, promptly notify applicant with Notice of Allowability (PTOL-37). If processing delays are expected, notify applicant via interview and send an Interview Summary (PTOL-413). Make every effort to mail notice before the period for reply expires to avoid unnecessary appeal or abandonment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consequences of no appeal and no allowable amendment
rubrics_metrics.description: If no appeal has been filed within the period for reply and no amendment has been submitted to make the application allowable or which can be entered in part, the application stands abandoned.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Filing of a 37 CFR 1.181 petition will not stay the period for reply to an examiner’s action.

rubrics_metrics.name: Form paragraph usage and specific advisory-paragraphs after final
rubrics_metrics.description: Specific form paragraphs (¶ 7.67–7.80, 7.51, etc.) are prescribed for use in advisory actions after final rejection, advisories when appeals have been filed, statements of proposed rejections on appeal, and explanations of nonentry.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examiners must follow prescribed form paragraph sequencing and bracket insertions for consistency (examples: 7.67 heading text for shortened statutory period, 7.69/7.70 for amendments entered for appeal, 7.71–7.76 for non-entry reasons).

rubrics_metrics.name: Reasons for refusal mapped to form paragraphs (e.g., 7.72–7.80)
rubrics_metrics.description: Specific refusal reasons map to standard form paragraphs: 7.72 (no convincing showing under 1.116(b)), 7.73 (raises new issues), 7.75 (form for appeal not improved), 7.76 (additional claims presented), 7.78 (proposed new claims would be allowable if submitted separately), 7.79 (affidavit/exhibit considered but insufficient), 7.80 (affidavit/exhibit not considered because no good reasons shown).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow required precedences (e.g., 7.71 must precede these paragraphs) and provide explanations or examples when new issues are extensive.

rubrics_metrics.name: Hand-delivery of papers to an examining group
rubrics_metrics.description: An examining group will accept a personally delivered paper only if: (1) the paper is accompanied by some form of receipt which can be handed back to the person delivering the paper; and (2) the examining group being asked to receive the paper is responsible for acting on the paper.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The receipt should identify applicant name(s), application number, filing date, and description of the paper(s). The paper and receipt will be date-stamped and the paper will be correlated with the application and made an official paper. If a paper is accompanied by a check or authorization to charge a Deposit Account, group personnel will hand-carry the paper to the Office of Finance for processing; accounting clerk will process for pickup by 3:00 p.m. next work day and papers will be entered in the application file wrapper.

rubrics_metrics.name: Expedited procedure for processing post-final amendments/replies (Box AF)
rubrics_metrics.description: To obtain expedited processing of amendments and replies under 37 CFR 1.116, applicants must mark the amendment or reply: “Reply under 37 CFR 1.116 — Expedited Procedure - Examining Group (Insert Examining Group Number)” on the upper right and mark the envelope “Box AF” in the lower left; the envelope should contain only replies under 37 CFR 1.116 and be mailed to “Box AF, Assistant Commissioner for Patents, Washington, D.C. 20231,” or be hand-carried and similarly marked.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Marked envelopes will be specially processed by the Mail Center and forwarded promptly; the SPE ensures prompt examiner action. PTO's goal is to mail the examiner’s action within 1 month from receipt. If no action is received within that time plus normal mailing, contact the SPE then the Group Director if necessary. Applicants not using the procedure will not obtain the expedited benefits.

rubrics_metrics.name: Amendments after allowance and Ex parte Quayle practice
rubrics_metrics.description: After all claims have been allowed, prosecution on the merits is closed (Ex parte Quayle). Amendments touching the merits after allowance are treated similarly to amendments after final rejection; amendments received after the notice of allowance have the status of 37 CFR 1.312 and their entry is a matter of grace.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If an amendment prepared prior to allowance reaches the Office after the notice of allowance has been mailed, it is treated as filed under 37 CFR 1.312. If received prior to mailing but not to the examiner until after mailing, it may have the same standing as though notice had not been mailed if the application has not been closed to further prosecution. Use form paragraph 7.51 (Quayle Action) to notify applicant of formal matters remaining and set a two-month shortened statutory period for reply.
